title: State and local officials charged with public corruption each year, and how many governments they serve
universe: Federal public corruption prosecutions of state and local officials by every United States Attorney's Office and the Public Integrity Section, compiled from annual surveys of the offices; local governments in the United States
limits: Federal prosecutions only: state attorneys general and local prosecutors charge others, so these counts are a floor on corruption that surfaced, not a count of all of it, and corruption no one exposed is not counted at all. Public corruption here is every offense the offices file as such (bribery, extortion, fraud and others), not bribery alone. A charge and a conviction in the same year need not be the same case. The state count includes officials of the District of Columbia and the territories, so it is divided by the game's 56 places, not 50 states. The counts are officials charged, not offenses or bribe incidents, so they are no lower bound on bribery and no band for bribes reported to the press: a played world's bribe counts are printed beside them as an exploratory proxy only. They are never a chance an engine reads.
quote: The figures in Tables I through III include all public corruption prosecutions within each district including cases handled by the United States Attorneys' Offices and the Public Integrity Section.
